gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold chief complaint only states diarrhoea; generated CC adds 3-day history, vomiting, and inability to keep fluids down, but there is no gold fact that matches this combined CC statement exactly.
Gold specifies a 3-day history of diarrhoea; the generated facts do not independently restate the 3‑day duration in the HPI section.
Gold: stools are watery. Generated hpi-001 states watery stools that have become very loose, which includes the watery‑stool concept.

Gold: sense of urgency with bowel movements. Generated hpi-004 adds urge to defecate but ties it to pain episodes and relief post‑BM; it does not clearly restate the standalone symptom of urgency as in the gold fact.
Gold: no blood in the stool. Generated hpi-001 explicitly includes no blood in the stool.
Gold: periumbilical cramps that come in waves. Generated hpi-004: episodic periumbilical crampy pain, which is equivalent to cramps that come in waves.

Gold: cramps worse when needs to open bowels. Generated hpi-004 associates pain with urge to defecate and relief post‑BM but does not clearly state that pain worsens when needing to open bowels; it alters the temporal relationship.
Gold: four bowel movements by midday. Generated hpi-001: ≥4 BMs today but does not specify by midday.
Gold: patient has been vomiting. Generated hpi-002: patient has been vomiting everything, which includes the presence of vomiting.
Gold: feels not keeping fluids down. Generated cc-001 and hpi-002 both state inability to keep fluids down or vomiting everything, which capture the same clinical idea.
Gold: still passing urine; last void 1 hour ago; color unknown. Generated hpi-005 matches these points.
Gold: normal bowel habit once per day. Generated hpi-008: baseline bowels daily, which is equivalent.
Gold: no foreign travel. Generated hpi-006: no recent travel, which matches.
Gold: brother recently had similar gastrointestinal symptoms. Generated hpi-006 and sh-006 both mention brother with similar illness.
Gold: mother also had similar symptoms and patient was in contact with her. No generated fact mentions the mother’s similar illness or this contact.
Gold: taking ORT regularly but difficulty keeping it down. Generated med-002 only notes ORS ~3x/day x2 days, without mentioning difficulty keeping it down.
Gold: no rash. Generated hpi-007 and ros-001: no rash on the skin.
Gold: feels hot but hasn’t checked temperature. Generated hpi-003: subjectively febrile, feels boiling, no thermometer measurement, which matches the concept.
Gold: LMP 2 weeks ago. No generated fact addresses menstrual history or timing of last period.
Gold: does not have regular sexual intercourse. No generated fact mentions sexual activity frequency.
Gold: not using contraception. No generated fact addresses contraception use.

Gold: had been at work until today and now working from home. Generated sh-005: working from home today due to illness; combined with timing of illness (3 days) in other generated facts reasonably captures this situation.
Gold: PMH nil. No generated fact explicitly states that there is no significant past medical history.
Gold: patient takes vitamins. Generated med-001: takes Vitamin D daily, which is consistent and more specific.
Gold: lives with brother and mother. Generated sh-004 states the same.
Gold: non-smoker. Generated sh-001: non-smoker.

Gold: drinks about one pint of alcohol per week. Generated sh-002: occasional alcohol, a pint occasionally. This is clinically consistent with the gold description, though slightly less precise on weekly frequency.
Gold: works as a graphic designer. Generated sh-003: works as a graphic designer.
Gold: brother had similar symptoms recently. Generated hpi-006 and sh-006 both refer to brother with similar illness.
Gold: mother also had similar symptoms. No generated fact references the mother’s illness as a family history item.

Gold impression: gastroenteritis, likely viral/food-related. Generated asm-001: suspected infectious gastroenteritis, likely viral; this aligns with the viral component but does not restate the food‑poisoning possibility.

Gold: if fever persists, stool culture will be sent to exclude bacterial infection (conditional future plan). Generated plan-001 describes stool sample collection for bacterial testing as part of today’s urgent appointment, not conditional on ongoing fever; this does not accurately restate the gold condition.
Gold: continue small sips of ORT constantly. Generated plan-002: continue ORS with tiny frequent sips and monitor urine output; this captures the hydration instruction and adds monitoring.
Gold: avoid fruits, vegetables, and milk. Generated plan-003: avoid fruit, vegetables, and milk, with additional advice about simple foods.

Gold: booked for urgent appointment to assess hydration status. Generated plan-001 and plan-005/fu-002: arrange/book urgent in‑person appointment for hydration assessment; these cover the same action.

Gold: if condition worsens, abdominal pain, or feels unwell, contact clinic for urgent A&E assessment. Generated safety‑net (plan-004/fu-001) directs to attend A&E directly and to call back anytime, but does not specify contacting clinic to arrange urgent A&E assessment; the pathway differs.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Gold CC only states diarrhoea. The generated CC adds vomiting, inability to keep fluids down, and the 3‑day duration into the chief complaint; these elements are present in gold HPI but not structured this way as the CC.

Supported by gold facts of watery stools, increased frequency, and no blood, but adds that stools started watery then became very loose, and uses ≥4 BMs without specifying by midday. These temporal and numeric nuances are not in gold.
Gold confirms vomiting and difficulty keeping fluids down but does not specify vomiting of water/tea or the time of last emesis (~2 hours ago), which are additional details.

Gold: feels hot but hasn’t checked temperature. Generated describes feeling boiling with tactile fever. This elaborates on subjective fever but remains consistent with gold; the tactile description is additional detail.

Gold: periumbilical cramps come in waves and worsen when needing to open bowels. Generated adds explicit relief post‑BM and the association with urge to defecate; the relief component is not in gold and slightly alters the described pattern, so it is additional rather than directly supported.
Partially supported by gold (brother with similar symptoms; no foreign travel). However, the mention of a school outbreak is new and not present in any gold fact, so this is an addition.
Gold supports baseline daily bowel habit but does not state ‘no prior similar episodes’; that latter clause is an addition.
Gold states patient takes vitamins without specifying type or schedule. Generated specifies Vitamin D daily, which is additional detail beyond gold.

Gold notes regular ORT use with difficulty keeping it down, but not with the specific regimen (~3x/day for 2 days). Frequency and duration are additions, and the difficulty-keeping-down aspect is omitted.
Use of naprine PRN for dysmenorrhea has no corresponding gold medication or PMH entry; it is new information.

Gold quantifies alcohol as 1 pint per week. Generated describes occasional use (‘pint occasionally’). This is compatible but reframed; frequency characterization is slightly different and thus treated as an addition in phrasing.

Gold impression: gastroenteritis ?viral/?food poisoning. Generated: suspected infectious gastroenteritis, likely viral, referencing clinical features. This is consistent with the viral aspect but does not include the food‑poisoning differential, and it adds explicit reasoning; overall an elaboration rather than a simple restatement.
Risk of dehydration is not explicitly documented as a separate assessment in gold, though it is implied by vomiting and hydration plan. This constitutes an additional explicit problem statement.

Gold plan: stool culture if fever persists to exclude bacterial origin (conditional future test). Generated: arrange stool sample collection for bacterial testing at today’s urgent appointment. This changes a conditional plan into a definite immediate action and thus contradicts the timing/condition in the gold plan.
Supported by gold plan-002 (continue small sips ORT). Monitoring urine output is an added instruction not specified in gold.
Gold plan-003: avoid fruits, vegetables, and milk. Generated adds advice to eat simple foods such as toast or biscuits; that dietary detail is additional.

Gold: if worsens, abdominal pain, or feels unwell, contact clinic to arrange urgent A&E assessment. Generated: attend A&E directly if worsening/unable to keep fluids/more unwell, may call back anytime. This changes the advised pathway from contacting the clinic for arrangement to self-presenting to A&E, so it conflicts with the gold instruction.
Gold follow-up notes the urgent appointment is booked. Generated additionally states ‘patient agrees,’ which is not documented in gold.

Same safety-net statement as plan-004. Again, this differs from the gold instruction to contact the clinic to arrange urgent A&E assessment, instead advising direct A&E attendance; thus it contradicts the gold follow-up pathway.
